title: Microsoft Teams: choose the institution type in the Teams for Education Policy Wizard
summary: The roadmap details and both wizard entry paths are supported. The policy-assignment guidance needs a qualification: existing educator and staff group policies do not necessarily override the wizard, which assigns its policies at the highest group ranking.

claims.claim: Roadmap item 402185 describes administrators selecting their institution's tenant type in the policy wizard and changing it later.
claims.quote: Admins can now select tenant type for their institution from the policy wizard. This setting can be changed anytime from the wizard.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is Launched.
claims.quote: "status": "Launched", "statusKey": "launched"

claims.claim: The roadmap target is November CY2024.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "November CY2024"

claims.claim: The roadmap record supplies no preview date.
claims.quote: "previewDate": null

claims.where: front matter: releasePhase; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The release phase is General Availability.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability"]

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope

claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.quote: "platforms": ["Desktop", "Mac", "Web"]

claims.claim: The roadmap modification timestamp is 2026-11-19T01:58:21.
The wizard sets policies based on the institution type, with options Primary or Secondary and Higher education.
claims.quote: The wizard sets up policies based on educational institution type (**Primary or Secondary** or **Higher education**).

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Scope; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: For students, the wizard changes the Global (Org-wide default) definitions in its covered policy areas.
claims.quote: The wizard adjusts the Global (Org-wide default) policy definition of each policy area covered by the wizard with new default settings that are appropriate to keep your students safe.

claims.claim: For educators and staff, the wizard creates custom policy definitions and assigns them to the selected groups.
claims.quote: The wizard creates a set of custom policy definitions for each policy area covered by the wizard with settings tailored to the needs of educators and staff. Then, it assigns the policy definitions to the group of educators and staff that you choose.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The wizard permits selecting up to three educator and staff groups.
claims.quote: You can select up to three groups.

claims.claim: Microsoft instructs administrators without educator and staff groups to create a group and rerun the wizard.
claims.quote: If you don't have any groups set up yet for your educators and staff, create a group, and then rerun the wizard.

claims.claim: The student policy areas are Teams, Meeting, Live events, App setup, App permission, Messaging and Calling.
claims.quote: Teams policy ... Meeting policy ... Live events policy ... App setup policy ... App permission policy ... Messaging policy ... Calling policy

claims.claim: The educator and staff custom policy areas are Teams, Meeting, Live events, Messaging and Calling.
claims.quote: Teams policy ... Meeting policy ... Live events policy ... Messaging policy ... Calling policy

claims.where: What's changing; controls[1].note; Why it matters
claims.claim: Changing only the institution type applies the Global policy definitions for the new type to students.
claims.quote: The Global (Org-wide default) policy definitions based on the new educational institution type are applied to students.

claims.claim: Changing only the institution type creates and assigns new custom definitions to the educator and staff groups.
claims.quote: A set of custom policy definitions based on the new educational institution type is created and assigned to the educators and staff groups.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Changing the institution type removes the previous type's custom policy definitions from educator and staff groups.
claims.quote: The custom policy definitions created for the previous educational institution type are removed from the educators and staff groups.

claims.claim: New Teams features receive EDU-relevant defaults in Global policies without further administrator intervention.
claims.quote: whenever a new feature is added to Teams, the appropriate EDU relevant default value of the policy for that feature will be automatically added to the Global (Org-wide default) without requiring any admin intervention.

claims.claim: Microsoft describes student policies as needing to be more restrictive.
claims.quote: Policies for students need to be more restrictive to reduce their risk of receiving inappropriate levels of access.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Existing direct or group assignments for students, educators and staff override the wizard's policies.
claims.quote: If your educators and staff group has an existing policy of the same policy area assigned to it, that existing policy is moved to a lower ranking and the policy assigned by the wizard takes effect.
claims.fix: Qualify the assignment statements in Risk assessment, Cost and licensing and Before rollout: 'For students, remove existing direct and group assignments so the Global policies take effect. For educators and staff, remove conflicting direct assignments; the wizard assigns its group policies at ranking 1, the highest ranking, and moves an existing policy on the selected group to a lower ranking.' Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/easy-policy-setup-edu#what-to-do-after-running-the-wizard.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The wizard's initial policy application is admin-opt-in through selecting Apply.
claims.quote: Select **Apply** to apply your changes.

claims.claim: The wizard starts automatically for administrators new to Teams.
claims.quote: If you're new to Teams, the wizard automatically starts.

claims.claim: Applying changes can take a few minutes, with Global definitions then applied immediately to students.
claims.quote: This may take a few minutes to complete.The Global (Org-wide default) policy definitions are immediately applied to students.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Educator and staff custom-policy assignments can take a few hours depending on group size.
claims.quote: For your educators and staff, it could take a few hours for the custom policies to be assigned to each member of the groups you selected, depending on the size of the groups.

claims.claim: No new data access is described for the institution-type selection.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams for Education Policy Wizard tenant type 402185 date data access licensing. Read the roadmap record and easy-policy-setup-edu in full; they describe policy configuration, not a new data-access grant.

claims.claim: Learn does not describe carrying edits from previous custom policies into the policies for a new institution type.
claims.quote: Searched: institution type wizard Graph Teams education. Read easy-policy-setup-edu, including Make changes in the wizard: it describes creating new definitions and removing previous assignments, with no edit-migration mechanism.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The first-run entry is Microsoft Teams admin center > Home > Easy policy setup for a safe learning environment > Quick setup, followed by institution-type selection.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Microsoft Teams admin center, go to **Home**, and then in the **Easy policy setup for a safe learning environment** tile, select **Quick setup**.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The change entry is Microsoft Teams admin center > Home > Easy policy setup for a safe learning environment > Change, followed by the wizard pages.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Microsoft Teams admin center, go to **Home**, and then in the **Easy policy setup for a safe learning environment** tile, select **Change**.

claims.claim: No PowerShell or API operation for the wizard's initial institution-type selection was found.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams education policy wizard institution type PowerShell Microsoft Graph Set-CsTeamsEducationConfiguration licensing requirements; institution type wizard Graph Teams education. Read Set-CsTeamsEducationConfiguration and the wizard page; no type-setting operation found.

claims.claim: No PowerShell or API operation for changing the wizard's institution type was found.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams education institution type PowerShell; institution type wizard Graph Teams education. Read Set-CsTeamsEducationConfiguration, wizard change instructions and Graph education overview excerpts; no operation changing the wizard's institution type found.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A wizard-specific licensing entitlement is not published in the documentation found, so its licensing model is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams for Education Policy Wizard licensing license requirements education A1 A3 A5; Teams for Education Policy Wizard license. Read wizard, teams-edu-licensing and Teams for Education prerequisites; product licenses are documented, but no wizard-specific entitlement is stated.

claims.where: controls[0].note; licensing.notes; Scope; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: The wizard's Learn page names no required administrator role.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams for Education Policy Wizard role prerequisites. Read easy-policy-setup-edu in full; it specifies the Teams admin center but no named required role. The education-configuration cmdlet's separate role requirement does not document this UI wizard.

claims.claim: Neither the wizard's Learn page nor the roadmap names a wizard licence or meter.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams for Education Policy Wizard licensing license requirements education A1 A3 A5; Teams for Education Policy Wizard license. Read easy-policy-setup-edu in full and the roadmap record; neither names a licence or meter.

claims.claim: The wizard's Learn page does not date the addition of institution-type selection.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams for Education Policy Wizard tenant type 402185 date data access licensing. Read easy-policy-setup-edu in full; its institution-type instructions give no date for introducing the selection.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends checking Message Center for new Teams features, policies and settings.
claims.quote: But do check the Message Center (in the Microsoft 365 admin center) frequently to stay up to date on new features and their policies and policy settings in Teams.

claims.claim: The documented wizard flow reviews selections before Apply.
claims.quote: 4. Review your selections.

claims.where: front matter: cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The known cost is low administrative effort, with wizard-specific licensing left unconfirmed rather than asserted free.
claims.quote: Select your educational institution type (**Primary or Secondary** or **Higher education**), and then select **Next**.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout and At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The checklist tells administrators to inventory and remove existing policy assignments, but the controls table covers only institution-type selection.
claims.quote: List existing direct and group policy assignments for students, educators and staff in each policy area, because they override the wizard's policies. / Institution type chosen on the first run of the wizard / Institution type changed after the wizard has run
claims.fix: The checklist's policy-assignment inventory and removal steps have no corresponding controls row. Narrow those checklist bullets to: 'Review the wizard documentation's after-run instructions for conflicting policy assignments.' Do not add a control row as part of this correction.

claims.claim: The sources checked do not say existing policies change if nobody runs the wizard.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Education Policy Wizard institution type easy-policy-setup-edu; Teams for Education Policy Wizard tenant type 402185 date data access licensing. Read the wizard page and roadmap: policy application is described through running the wizard and selecting Apply.
